description.narrative: Stakeholders Impact: Improved access to finance for to women borrowers: IFC anticipates that the proposed investment will help increase access to finance to WMSMEs. The MSME finance gap is estimated to be over US$300 billion, equivalent to roughly 13% of GDP. WMSMEs tend to suffer more from higher perceived risk by formal financial institutions. WMSMEs face a finance gap estimated at US$29 billion, equivalent to about 1% of Indias GDP, and almost 10% of the total MSME finance gap in the country. The Project will help MMFSL to provide much needed finance to underserved WMSMEs who need financing for income generation purposes. Market Impact: IFC anticipates that via demonstration and replication channels, the Project will promote greater inclusiveness in the broader MSME financing market by encouraging other NBFCs, especially those operating in the vehicle financing space, to scale-up their lending to WMSMEs. Further, women entrepreneurs in India face a rejection rate of 19% by lending institutions, more than twice the rate of 8% for men and approximately 90% of women entrepreneurs in India have not availed financing from formal FIs and rely often on riskier informal sources primarily due to the lack of collateral required by formal institutions. IFC anticipates that by supporting MMFSLs commitment to expanding the Companys WMSME portfolio in rural areas, the Project will demonstrate to peer NBFCs the business case for lending to this underserved segment, ultimately resulting in higher access to finance for women entrepreneurs in India.

The proposed project envisages a secured funding in Mahindra and Mahindra Financial Services Limited (MMFSL or the Company) of up to US$200 million or INR equivalent, for growing its portfolio of loans to micro, small & medium enterprises (MSMEs). 100% of IFCs investment will be earmarked for on-lending to women-owned MSMEs (WMSMEs) in rural areas.
